questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose the best smartphone for children
Why adults spend too long on email
Whether children are better off without smartphones
How social media companies make money
questions.why: They ask whether kids are better off without a phone.

questions.q: Why does Beth not answer Neil at the start?
options: She is on a phone call
She is busy checking her social media and email
She can't hear him
She is reading an interesting article in a magazine
questions.why: She was checking Instagram and Facebook and sending an email, so Neil thinks she's addicted.

questions.q: What do studies show about smartphones and young people?
options: Girls who use social media more are more often anxious or depressed
Smartphones help children sleep better
Children who use phones every day do much better at school than others
Boys are more affected than girls
questions.why: Neil says girls who spend more time on social media are more likely to be anxious or depressed.

questions.q: How many British eight-to-eleven-year-olds have a smartphone?
options: About 10%
About 30%
Almost all of them
Around 60%
questions.why: Beth says around 60% of British eight-to-eleven-year-olds have a smartphone.

questions.q: What worries journalist Myra Anubi about giving her daughter a phone?
options: How much time she'll spend on it and what she might see
The cost of the phone
That she might lose it or break it at school during the day
That she'll stop doing homework
questions.why: She's worried about how much time her daughter will spend on it and what she might see.

questions.q: How does Myra feel about the decision?
options: Sure that her daughter should have a phone
Sure that her daughter should never have one until she is much older
Not worried at all
Torn, because she doesn't want her daughter to feel left out
questions.why: She says she's 'torn', because some of her daughter's friends already have smartphones.

questions.q: What did Daisy Greenwell and Clare Fernyhough's WhatsApp group encourage parents to do?
options: Buy their children phones earlier
Wait until 14 for a smartphone and 16 for social media
Ban phones in all schools
Only let children use phones at weekends and never after school
questions.why: It encouraged no smartphone until 14 and no social media access until 16.

questions.q: What happened after Daisy posted about the group on social media?
options: Most parents criticised the idea, so the group soon stopped meeting at all
The group was closed
It spread quickly, and now over 100,000 people in the UK are involved
Only a few local families joined
questions.why: She says it went viral, groups sprang up all over the country, and there are now over 100,000 people.
